cost of maintaining a landscaped berm and the extensive land required for it would appear to be a disadvantage inherent in the berm approach. We recognize that a berm located as shown in the Statement has the value of shielding the neighborhood from the noise of traffic on Grayland Avenue; however, there may be some obstruction of vision at intersections which could be avoided by the use of a wall on the north side of Grayland Avenue. Obviously, comparative costs and the feasibility of adapting a wall structure to the location and grade of the slopes required for the Downtown Expressway must be examined before a valid comparison can be made. We endorse in principal the concept of shielding the Randolph neighborhood from the noise of traffic on the Expressway and simply take this opportunity to suggest that the final Statement present the landscaped berm as one means of accomplishing that objective without precluding development of more desirable alternatives.
The only other adverse impact which the Statement suggests might be mitigated is the matter of light spill on adjacent areas from the Downtown Expressway. The Statement acknowledges the various views of residents, both pro and con, which might be anticipated. Furthermore, the cost and availability of specialized lighting fixtures and the effects on traffic safety resulting from reduction in the level of illumination on the Expressway are unknown at this time. The City Administration will review with the Richmond Metropolitan Authority alternatives which appear feasible and desirable in view of the various considerations involved. It is my hope that a solution will be possible which minimizes adverse environmental effects without limiting traffic safety.
Several minor errors are noted in the report as follows:
1. Descriptions of Areas (1) and (2) are transposed on pages 9 and 10.
2. The bridge indicated for Lombardy Street in the illustration on page 17 is not correct and should be deleted.
3. The first line of A (3) contains the word "with" which should be changed to "will" in order to convey the proper meaning.
